items.stem: During which stroke of a four-stroke petrol engine does the spark plug normally fire to initiate combustion?

options.text: At the end of the intake stroke
options.rationale: Firing during intake would ignite an incomplete, uncompressed charge.

options.text: Near the end of the compression stroke
options.rationale: Ignition occurs shortly before top dead centre on compression so peak pressure arrives just after TDC on the power stroke.
The exhaust stroke expels burned gas; igniting then does no useful work.

options.text: At bottom dead centre of the power stroke
options.rationale: That is far too late; the useful expansion would already be lost.

items.explanation: Ignition occurs shortly before top dead centre on compression so peak pressure arrives just after TDC on the power stroke.

items.stem: An engine runs with lambda = 1.0. What does this indicate about the air-fuel mixture?

options.rationale: Lambda = 1.0 means the actual air-fuel ratio equals the stoichiometric ratio.

options.text: The mixture is rich with excess fuel
options.rationale: A rich mixture gives lambda below 1.0.

options.text: The mixture is lean with excess air
options.rationale: A lean mixture gives lambda above 1.0.

options.text: There is no fuel being injected
options.rationale: Zero fuel would not produce a defined lambda of 1.0.

items.explanation: Lambda = 1.0 means the actual air-fuel ratio equals the stoichiometric ratio.

items.stem: A technician observes engine knock under load. Select TWO changes that would typically reduce the tendency to knock.

options.rationale: Later ignition lowers peak in-cylinder pressure and temperature, reducing end-gas auto-ignition.
Higher octane resists auto-ignition, directly reducing knock under load.
Raising compression increases end-gas pressure and temperature, worsening knock.

options.text: Lean the mixture significantly at high load
options.rationale: Leaning at high load raises combustion temperatures and tends to increase knock.
Wheel size does not affect in-cylinder combustion conditions.

items.explanation: Later ignition lowers peak in-cylinder pressure and temperature, reducing end-gas auto-ignition.
